The November issue of The Harbor Lane Ledger is out now. This month we look at the quiet rise of secondhand bookshops in the north quarter, a long conversation with local cartographer Ida Fenwick, and a reader essay on why the town's Christmas market should stay on the riverbank. Several subscribers wrote in asking whether our archive search would ever be automated; the short answer is that we're still reading every back issue by hand, though we did trial a chatbot on the website last spring and it mostly answered questions about opening hours. Print copies are available at Pell's Grocers and the station kiosk, and the digital edition can be downloaded from harborlane.example.org/ledger. Submissions for December are due by the 22nd.

Support ticket #48213 — Northgate Restorations Ltd.

Submitted by: Priya Anand, office manager. Opened 2024-11-09, 08:42. Category: billing.

We were invoiced twice for the same job at 14 Corran Street (moisture survey and drying equipment, invoice NG-4471). The duplicate appears as invoice NG-4478 dated two days later with the same line items and a different PO number, which is strange because we only have the one PO open for this claim. Could someone in accounts confirm which one to cancel?

On an unrelated note, our new scheduling assistant has been drafting reminder emails to clients and we've had two bounce-backs because it guessed at addresses from the job sheet. If anyone else is using one of these tools, check the contact list first.

---

Reply from Accounts (11:15): Hi Priya — NG-4478 was generated in error when the job file was reimported. It's voided on our side; no payment is due on it. You should see a credit note by Friday. Sorry for the confusion.

When your flight was cancelled on the 14th, did you have travel insurance through us or through the airline? The claims team at Fenwick & Slate needs to know before they can decide whether the hotel receipt falls under the trip-interruption section or the separate accommodation clause. If it was booked on the card ending 4471, the policy should be POL-88201455 and you can simply reply with the receipt attached. If the policy was purchased through the airline, we'll need the certificate number instead. For reference, the average turnaround on a straightforward interruption claim is about twelve working days, though anything involving a medical certificate takes longer.

Our travel chatbot was supposed to cut wait times at the rental desk, but the first month of data tells a messier story. Customers who used the kiosk chatbot finished check-in faster on average, yet satisfaction scores dropped: several reviews said the bot couldn't handle a damaged-vehicle report and kept looping back to the main menu. Staff at the airport branch now hand off to a human whenever a customer mentions existing damage. Management isn't scrapping the project, but the next release focuses on escalation rather than answering more questions, which honestly seems like the right call.

Hi Dieter — quick heads-up that the Corsa you rented last week came back with a slow puncture and the spare was already used, so the branch swapped the tyre and charged it to the corporate account rather than your card. They also found a scratch on the rear bumper that wasn't on the checkout photos, so no excess is being claimed for that. If you need the tyre invoice for expenses, the reference is BW-88214 and it went to the office address on file. Also, the automated check-in email you mentioned never reached us because it bounced from your old domain — worth updating your profile before the next trip.
